name: Triangular pyramid volume
seoDesc: Triangular pyramid volume: work out base (b) from the base height and the side c. A free math calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Triangular pyramid volume calculator turns the base height, the side c and more into base (b). It suits a homework check, a spreadsheet build or a bit of mental arithmetic you want to confirm. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Triangular pyramid volume calculator work?
sections.html:
The Triangular pyramid volume calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports base (b) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the triangle type); then you type in the base height (h), the side c, the side a (2) and the angle γ.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Triangular pyramid volume calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Base (b)=2 × pyramid base area ÷ base height (h)
Side b=2 × pyramid base area ÷ (side a × the sine of (angle γ))
Side b=the square root of ((side a ^ 2) + (side c ^ 2) + 2 × the square root of (-4 × (pyramid base area ^ 2) + (side a ^ 2) × (side c ^ 2)))
Pyramid base area=(1 ÷ 2) × (side a ^ 2) × the sine of (angle β) × the sine of (angle γ) ÷ the sine of (angle β + angle γ)
Pyramid height (H)=3 × volume ÷ pyramid base area (A)
Pyramid height (H)=3 × volume ÷ pyramid base area

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Triangular pyramid volume calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Splitting a bill, a measurement or a shape problem between several people
  • Settling an argument about a number with a quick, traceable result
  • Checking a homework answer before you hand it in
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the base height, the side c and the side a — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Triangular pyramid volume calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns base (b), derived from the base height, the side c and the side a. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Triangular pyramid volume calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the base height, the side c, the side a and the angle γ, which is 15 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter base (b) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Base (b) opens in centimeters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Triangular pyramid volume calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
